A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same longitudinal NLP study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original PTSD-STOP prediction experiments, including evaluation-split comparisons, representation/history analyses, and comparisons of temporal models.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Table 2, Figures 1–9, and the accompanying main-text and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The RoBERTa representations, PCA/ridge pipeline, autoregressive model, averaged-history model, causal transformer, and training objective remain unchanged. The new missingness discussion introduces no implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 238-participant, 17,051-document PTSD-STOP cohort, 20-person demonstration subset, and nowcasting/forecasting tasks. Newly mentioned HH-RLHF and Value Kaleidoscope datasets are motivational examples, not evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same typical model and training-mean baseline. The autoregressive, bag-of-embeddings, and transformer comparisons also retain identical membership; newly cited methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendices B–D retain the same cohort construction, split ratios and temporal cutoffs, development-set tuning, representation/history settings, and evaluation metrics. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The representation-size and history-length analyses, temporal-model comparisons, and Appendix C.2 checks concerning positional embeddings and training history are retained unchanged. The added missingness discussion contains no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same one-sided paired t-tests in Table 2 and standard-error displays and discussion for the modeling results. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice is added.

E6.justification: Original experimental results are unchanged. Table 2 retains model/baseline MAEs of .520/.660, .757/.619, and .455/.598 across its three settings; Figure 1's values and all subsequent plotted results also match.

T1.justification: Person/time indexing, the metric-scope definitions in Table 3, and the SMAPE and Pearson formulas in Appendix D are unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims the first systematic NLP demonstration of misleading or reversed conclusions from random splits and flattened metrics, and describes target-aligned evaluation as established best practice needing wider adoption. The abstract, five listed contributions, and conclusion otherwise retain their substantive claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds recommendations to preserve person/time identifiers and treat missingness as behavioral signal, developing v1's existing missingness caveat. It also extends the discussion to RLHF/value annotations, while Limitations identifies instruction-tuned LLM evaluation as future work.

D1.justification: Implementation, preprocessing, hyperparameters, and access/release information remain unchanged. v2 names the approving institutions and explicitly states informed consent, but secure handling was already disclosed in v1; these additions do not change technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 expands connections to personalization, RLHF/value annotation, ecological validity, temporal user modeling, and missing-data research. It adds citations including Bai, Salemi, Lipton, and Che, removes Kumar and Carley and Sawhney, and sharpens novelty around empirical demonstration while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: Several introduction paragraphs are rewritten or reordered, and localized additions expand Dataset, Discussion, Related Work, and Limitations. The overall section sequence, abstract, contribution list, and most experimental and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays are repositioned during text reflow, notably Table 3 moving from the left to the right column and Figure 2 moving higher in the right column. Graphics, axes, legends, captions, and table contents are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 better acknowledges established evaluation practices, develops practical recommendations about identifiers and missingness, and makes institutional approval and consent more explicit. These provide limited gains in context and transparency. The experiments and appendices remain unchanged, and the broader RLHF/LLM implications remain untested.
